notes:
CIRCUIT: a single-loop ladder drawn between a top rail (y~370, x 238..896) and a bottom rail (y~590, x 238..907), enclosed in a hand-drawn page border that is not a conductor. Reading left to right along the top: V-AC3 (6 sin(9t+10 deg) V) rises from the bottom rail to the top rail at x~238; R0 (54 kOhm) spans x 309..438; the node at x~489 drops to V-AC5 (9cos(9t) V) and back to the bottom rail; L1 (55 mH) spans x 576..688; then the right-hand section carries C2 (5 uF) dropping at x~779 and I-AC4 (7 sint A) dropping at x~896, both returning to the bottom rail. The single GND hangs off the bottom rail at x~615.

NET MAP:
  0  = bottom rail y~590 from x~238 to x~907, plus the GND stub at x~615: bottom of V-AC3, bottom of V-AC5, bottom of C2, bottom of I-AC4, GND6.
  n1 = top-left segment: top lead of V-AC3 (x~238, riser y 428..370) and the left lead of R0 at (309,364).
  n2 = top-middle segment x~438..576 at y~372: right lead of R0, left lead of L1, and the top lead of V-AC5 which drops away at site S6.
  n3 = top-right segment x~688..896: right lead of L1, top lead of C2 (drops at site S7), top lead of I-AC4.

SITE DECISIONS (all four CRITICAL sites plus S7 recorded explicitly):
  S6 (489,372) deg=3, dot=1.6, hop=0: a plain tee. The top rail runs straight left-right; a single stroke leaves it downward toward V-AC5 and there is no ink above the rail at this x. One wire ending on another is a junction. If it were read as anything else, V-AC5's top lead would sit on a one-terminal net and the source would drive nothing.
  S7 (769,379) deg=3, dot=1.6: same geometry - the top rail continues left-right and C2's lead drops away below it. Junction. Not flagged CRITICAL by the tracer only because C2's t0 was mis-assigned to label ink at the time; after the port fix this site is what puts C2's top on n3, so it is recorded here deliberately.
  S11 (779,587) deg=3, dot=2.1: C2's bottom lead arrives from above and terminates on the bottom rail, which continues both ways. Tee, and the drafter thickened the corner. Junction.
  S14 (500,595) deg=3, dot=1.6: V-AC5's bottom lead terminates on the bottom rail. Tee. Junction.
  S15 (615,596) deg=4, dot=1.1: the GND symbol's stub leaves the bottom rail downward; deg=4 because the skeleton splits the rail into two stubs each side of the contact point. Junction. Reading S11/S14/S15 as anything but junctions would sever the return path of C2, V-AC5 or the ground reference respectively - each of those is electrically impossible (a source or a branch with no return, and GND stranded on a one-terminal net), so these are forced regardless of ink.
  Non-critical sites S0 (388,332), S1 (416,335), S2 (687,335), S4 (676,335), S8 (731,442) and S10 (556,505) are all handwritten value text ('54 kOhm', '55 mH', '5 uF', '9cos(9t) V') brushing a component box or the rail above it. Left at default; none of them changes the netlist.

PORT FIXES (both were one-terminal nets caused by the terminal landing on value-label ink):
  - C2.t0 was on a stroke of the '5 uF' text at (742,432); moved to p1 (773,425), the real top lead (wire 44), which runs up to the top rail at S7 and so joins n3.
  - V-AC3.t0 was on the 'V' of '6 sin(9t+10 deg) V' at (189,476); moved to p1 (238,428), the real top lead (wire 139) - the same wire the resistor's left lead already used, which is why n1 previously had only R0.t0 on it.
  R0, L1, I-AC4, V-AC5 and GND6 already pointed at real leads and were left alone. All parts are two-terminal, so terminal order is unscored and the defaults are kept.

CLASSES: all seven match the drawn symbols - Resistor (zigzag, '54 kOhm'), Inductor (coil, '55 mH'), Capacitor (two plates, '5 uF'), two V-AC (circle with sine, '6 sin(9t+10 deg) V' and '9cos(9t) V'), I-AC (circle with sine plus a downward current arrow, '7 sint A'), GND. Note #4 is correctly I-AC rather than V-AC: the ellipse contains both a tilde and a large arrow, and its label is in amperes. No re-classification.

UNRESOLVED: nothing. Final netlist is 7 components / 4 nets, every terminal on a multi-terminal net, ERC clean.
